utterances.text: You knew Mr. Hadziosmanovic. Could you tell us first whether he played a role in the distribution of weapons which reached that place in the explained manner?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I personally know Dr. Hadziosmanovic. I read his book, and he was another person who was included in this project.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Bozic, on page 66 -- we do not have the time to read through everything that is stated there, but on page 66, please read the sentence which starts: "The police reserve forces, by being activated ..." This would be the last page, in the English translation, penultimate paragraph. Could you read out?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: "Reserve force of the police, by being activated, allowed for large quantities of weapons to be procured, as well as means of communication which were, per establishment, distributed to the reserve police force, the Patriotic League and the Croatian defenders. A large contribution to the organisation of the reserve police force and the Patriotic League and the ranks of Croatian defences was provided by Alija Delimustafic, Avdo Hebib, Slobodan Bozic, Jusuf Pusina, Bruno Stojic, Brana Kvesic, Ivica Lucic, Viktor Stojcic, Zikrija Djonko, Sejo Celebic, Ornica Djukic, Petar Zelenika, and Franjo Doko. These were Muslim and Croatian officials at the then regional MUP at Mostar and employees of the MUP of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So, Mr. Bozic, this excerpt from this book corroborates that high-ranking Muslim and Croatian officials took part in that, both at MUP Mostar and the MUP of the government of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: That's correct. I've already stated this to be so.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now I'm going to ask you to go through -- briefly through some documents which are supposed to corroborate what you stated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, this seems to be an important document, and I have to ask you an additional question. This book was written by Dr. Ismet Hadziosmanovic. I guess he's a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This book was published in September 2006 in Mostar. If we are to believe page 3 in the English translation, we observe that -- I don't need months or years to get prepared. You know, it just takes me a few seconds and I understand everything. I discover that after the attack in April 1991 in Pitovic [phoen], a JNA attack, there was a meeting of all the SDA leaders of the Capljina and Jablanica municipalities, et cetera; and then we can see that at the level of the Patriotic League, a force was created. If you read further, you realise that rifles or weapons were brought by Croat friends from the Citluk Crisis Staff. You turn over to the next page and you realise that, in fact, Croats and Muslims are very much together, that an entity is being created that there's going to be an independent battalion to be set up with -- two at Tuplina [phoen], and also there's going to be a battalion and the HVO command in Mostar is going to be the Petar Zelenika Battalion. So just reading these few pages, one gets the impression that back then, Muslims and Croats are united against the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I could tell you that the Croats and the Muslims were united, standing together then, against anybody who jeopardised their survival there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it was important to know that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Bozic, let's go back to page 66 of the book. I'd like to ask you another question. Two paragraphs above, mention is made of the government's decision on activating the reserve police force. Could you recall, since you worked at the MUP in Mostar, when was this and what were the reasons for this happening?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Which part should I read?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: No, no, no, I didn't instruct you to read. I'm explaining that this is the same book, a paragraph which His Honour Antonetti read out to you. My question is: After the reservists came to Mostar in 1991, did the MUP of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina take a decision to activate the reserve police force because this is the topic of this book?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: This was only logical, given the circumstances, the situation, out on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Let's go through some documents which demonstrate your positions and posts that you held from the beginning of your engagement with the HVO and the Department of Defence. First take a look at the document P 00921.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: These are minutes from the 15th session of the Croatian Defence Council of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, dated 17th of December. Please take a look at the last page, which reads -- it's under an asterisk which reads: "In the Commission for the Relations with UNPROFOR, apart from Mr. Zuko, S. Bozic and Mr. Sivric are going to be appointed."

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is what I testified about at the beginning. This is my first appointment which I had within the HVO of the HZ-HB.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now let's take a look at document P 00924, which follows, and this is a decision on the establishment of the Commission.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: I can see it. This is exactly what we made reference to just now. This decision specifies the jurisdiction of that commission.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber, and we will discuss that a bit later, what those duties were? And if necessary, we can read it.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: That we are setting up cooperation and relations with official representatives, that we're representing the HZ-HB, that we are coordinating the works of other organs and body with the UNPROFOR, and we are doing other tasks and assignments in this area. I did read this out, but it wasn't quite correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much. That is enough. Perhaps we can look at the next document. This is 2D 00978.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is Mr. Stojic's proposal to appoint me as the deputy head, and it was issued on the 13th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let's look at the next page of that document.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: This is a decision published in the Official Gazette, where it is stated that I am being appointed as deputy head.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. There's no need to look at this document any longer. We can look at the next one. That's P 0037 -- P 1137. It is the session of the Croatian Defence Council of the 15th of January, the 18th session of the council.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... understand why Ms. Nozica goes speedily, but I'm looking at your appointment on the 30th of January, 1993. You were appointed by Mr. Stojic. But on the left-hand side, I can see proposal accepted by the HVO HZ-HB at 11.00 on the 15th of January. During a session. I am now checking the B/C/S version to see whether that mentions also figures there. Witness, does this mean that appointments -- well, with regard to appointments, does it mean that something suggests that someone is appointed, somebody like you, for instance; but it had to be approved by a college of people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The initiative for any appointment would go from the organ that it referred to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter cannot hear the witness because of rustling.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- but the decision on the appointment was adopted by the HVO HZ-HB.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, this collective body could have said, No, we don't agree; and then Mr. Stojic would have been forced to suggest somebody else ?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is possible, also.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. President, one intervention. P 00924 has been mistranslated, if you see on the very first part, which is: "I hereby pass the following decision," and you see down at the signature line it would be Jadranko Prlic. It would give the impression that it was Prlic's decision that he passed it. I'm told by my colleague, Mrs. Ana Tomanovic, that there's no such thing as "I hereby pass." It just says, "Pass the following decision," in other words the collective body passes and not "I hereby," meaning Dr. Jadranko Prlic, and I think this is an area of contention.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I must admit that I did not understand --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, please. It might be good to read the text in Croatian, and then the interpreters would translate it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise, but I think that my colleague Mr. Karnavas reacted to P 00924. This is the decision on the establishment of the Commission or Office of the HVO HZ-HB on liaison with the UNPROFOR. So this is document P 00924. I didn't quite understand what the remark was about, but it doesn't matter. The witness can read it out, and the interpreters can then translate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Witness, if you would be so kind and just read the first paragraph, the introduction of document 0924. Some of it seems to be illegible. Don't worry about that. Just skip it or say that two or three words, or whatever, are illegible.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before entering the courtroom, I asked the usher if I'm able to use the marker, which helps me to see better, so now I'm going to try to read it better: "On the basis of Article 19 of the statutory decision about the temporary organisation of executive authority and administration in the area of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, at the session of the 17th of December, 1992 --" To tell you the truth, all I can see here are the letters d-o-n-o-s, so I don't know if it refers to the singular or the plural.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The French booth says "donos," "takes or makes the decision to," so there's a decision between "it is adopted" or, "I adopt." Witness, if we understand this, Mr. Prlic decided to appoint three individuals, including you, number 2, to his commission, but does this decision have to be adopted, endorsed, by the collective body during this session that took place on the 17th of December, 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the preamble of the decision, I can see the word "session of the 17th of December, 1992."

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can assist the Trial Chamber and the witness. We have already looked at this transcript from the meeting, and this is P 00921; and it can be seen that the decision was adopted at the meeting of the HVO HZ-HB. Is there anything that is disputable still?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, look, we're going to shed some light on this thanks to you, Witness. When you were appointed, was your appointment the outcome of the power invested in one single individual or in a collective body? This is a very clear question, you see.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to answer very clearly. These decisions, this one and any other decision, is adopted by the collective body, and it is signed by the person who is the president of that collective body.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need to avoid any mistake in interpretation. You said that the decision was made by a collective body, and it was signed by the person presiding over the collective body. At least that has the merit of being clear. You are a lawyer. You were a prosecutor and a judge. Therefore, what you say can be understood.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would just like to go back for a moment to document 2D 00978. It says here: "Proposal for appointment," signed by Mr. Stojic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And you, Witness, explained that Mr. Stojic proposed that and that the HVO HZ-HB adopted that decision. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is exactly what I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let's look how this decision was adopted by the HVO HZ-HB. Let's look at P 1137, and we can look at a paragraph marked number 7. So, as I said, this is the 18th session of the Croatian Defence Council. Under 7, it says: "Upon the proposal of the implementation of the law on the legal profession on the territory HZ-HB during the war." Mr. Bozic, I'm going to ask you to look at the next document, P 69. This is a document of the 1st of December, 1993, and it is the decision appointing you as the head of the Office for Cooperation with UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is the decision on my appointment which I referred to at the beginning when I spoke about why I continued to work after Mr. Stojic had left the Defence Department, with the remark that I was still continuing to work on my duties at the Personnel Administration.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. Let's look at the next document, P 770 -- 7790.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P 6696 might be interesting.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: 6996, interpreter's correction and apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There it is. This is a document appointing you to the position of the chief of the Cooperation Office with the UNPROFOR, so this is important. In the preamble, it can be seen that, in fact, it's not Mr. Prlic who appointed you. It was the government, the HR-HB government. Look at the preamble. Is that what the preamble says? Apparently it was discussed by the government on the 1st of December, 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this is what I said about the previous appointment. All appointments, as I said, are made at the sessions of the HVO HZ-HB, and now at the government meetings of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, and then the actual decisions on the appointment itself is signed by Mr. Prlic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are we to understand that it was Mr. Prlic who drafted the text or just signed it to authenticate the appointment decided upon by the government?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree, yes, it's part of his authority, he's at the head of that body, but the actual decision is made by the collective body.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The next document is P 07790, where you are being -- actually, the decision on the establishment of the Committee for Cooperation with the United Nations is adopted. You're one of the members. Can you please tell us whether you, as a member of this committee, and while working in it, did it have any important activities in 1994?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Well, perhaps -- no, as far as I can remember, we had two or three meetings. That's what I remember attending.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let's look at the next document. This is 2D 1006.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is a pass granting the transport of material and equipment. It's dated the 30th of June, 1992, and it's signed by assistant to the commander for logistics, Bruno Stojic. Is this absolutely in accordance with what you said, Mr. Bozic, that before being appointed as the head of the Defence Department, Mr. Stojic worked as assistant to the commander for logistics at the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you please look at the next document. This is document P 00297. And this is an appointment of Mr. Stojic as head of the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let's look at the next document. This is P 006583. And this is a press release dated the 10th of November, 1993, referring to members of the -- members of government of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: This is what I said at the beginning, from which -- and then from that point in time Mr. Stojic no longer came to the Defence Department, and about the way he found out about this appointment.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. And the last document in this first part, this is 2D 00416. It's a protocol signed by Mr. Jukic and by Mr. Bruno Stojic five days after this press release.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: I said at the beginning that I was not present at the signing and I did not see Mr. Stojic then. This is the first time that I am seeing the protocol, but it does confirm that it was the protocol about the hand-over of duty between Mr. Jukic and Mr. Stojic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bozic. You've already said at the beginning of your testimony that on arrival at the Defence Department, you took part in the drafting of some establishment documents?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'm now going to ask you specifically if in any way you participated in the adoption of regulations on the armed forces of the HZ-HB, adopted at the Presidency meeting of the 3rd of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: No, because I came to the department in September 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You also said that you participated in the drafting of a revised text about the armed forces of the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't catch the date.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, there was a consolidated text, pursuant to a section which was actually just added on, and there was some very minor changes in terms of the previously-adopted documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, let us now prepare for the next set of documents by saying that after the president of the HZ-HB, in September 1992, decided -- adopted a decision on establishing the Defence Department, and he referred to the sections which would be part of it and what their duties would be, and you worked on a document which was a document of the Defence Department.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you please tell us which parts of the documents you actually worked on?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: You are talking about the regulations of the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: No, I'm talking about the organisational documents of the Defence Department.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: I said in the beginning that I worked on the decision about the establishment of the Defence Department pursuant to a decision on the basic founding, which was adopted by Mr. Boban.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Sir, let us look at the following documents. These are documents P 00289. It's a regulation on the armed forces of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. I'm going to ask you to look at Article 10 of this rule, and if you can tell me, pursuant to this Article 10, paragraph 1, the duties of the Defence Department were referred to.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: It says here that the Defence Department performs professional and administrative assignments from defence and security, and then it refers to 25 specific tasks.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: According to your understanding, do these 25 points represent the professional and administrative tasks in the domain of defence and protection?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let us now look at document 2D 01262. These are minutes from the fifth session of the Presidency of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. You were not present at this session?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: No. You can see that the Defence Department was represented by Mr. Bozo Rajic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now I'm going to look at paragraph 17 or item 17 of the agenda where it says that the regulations on the armed forces was adopted at this meeting.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes, the proposals were adopted for the amendment and changes of these regulations, and Mr. Stojic discusses this -- I'm sorry, Mr. Buntic talks about the adoption of this regulation, describing that the amendments specifically refer to mobilisation, which were not previously discussed.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You're talking about comments on page 17; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is page 14 in the Croatian and 16 in the English?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: No. On my copy, it is page 15.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It begins, actually, on page 14; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes, but what I read about Mr. Buntic and the regulation of armed forces was on the 15th.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Okay. So we can conclude that the regulation on armed forces was adopted on that session. Previously we heard that you had taken part in drafting it with lawyers from the Justice Department, and now let's take a look at Article 10 in that regulation. Could you tell the Chamber whether this article remained unchanged?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: You mean the Official Gazette?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I apologise, apologise. It's P 00588, document P 00588, regulation on the armed forces, my mistake, dated 17th October 1993.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Which page, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Page 7. There are some parts which do not refer to the situation.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: I find it --

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Fine. Is that the regulation?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: This is the consolidated version of the regulation with the supplements and amendments that we discussed.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Please find for me Article 10.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Could you tell the Chamber whether it was amended or supplemented compared to the previous version, and does it specify the tasks of the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Bozic, now I'm going to ask you, since you said that you took part in drafting the consolidated version, to explain to the Chamber Article 34. What was the proposal that came from you to the Presidency, and whether it remained intact in the version that we can see here?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: When I was comparing the two, there is only one change, saying that certain appointments, instead of HVO HZ-HB, is done by head of department. But taking a look at the integral text of Article 34, obviously errors occurred when the Official Gazette was printed. It would only be logical, and it's clear when taking a look at the previous version of that article, that the original text should read: "Commanders of the armed forces shall be appointed and relieved by ...," and then, colon: "President of the HZ-HB, commanders of --" full stop. "Commanders of brigades and high-ranking officers," comma, not colon but comma, "head of the Defence Department and commanders authorised to do so by him. Other officers and commanders, junior officers and military personnel ...," et cetera, et cetera. So the problem that arises is the part which discusses commanders of brigades and high-ranking officers. It shouldn't contain a comma, but a full stop, and the comma should be after the "President of HZ-HB," and "the commanders appointed by him," there should be a comma, and to be followed by "other officers and commanders, junior officers, and military personnel shall also be appointed to posts of officers, junior officers in the armed forces."

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Bozic, if I understand you correctly, the president of the HZ-HB, as you construed it, appoints commanders of brigades and high-ranking officers; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, and this is where the full stop should be.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And then head of the Defence Department and officers --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Head of Defence Department and commanders authorised by him will appoint other officers, commanders, junior officers?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Bozic, could you tell us how this mistake occurred? As I understood you, you prepared a consolidated, clear version of the text and sent it for approval to the Presidency. Could you -- and then these mistakes occurred. Can you explain how?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Well, at that time we did not have any floppy discs or information communication technology and equipment that we have today. Our consolidated draft was written on an electric typewriter, and, as such, it went to the printing shop. And then at the print shop, they had to transcribe that into their system, and I'm sure that the preparation for printing was when those mistakes occurred. And this can be verified if you take a look at the provision of Article 34 in the basic regulation on armed forces and compare it to this one.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: When you say "basic regulation," you're referring to the July 7th 1992 regulation?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: That's P 00789; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now I'm going to ask you, furthermore: Mr. Bozic, did the Personnel Administration, which was part of your civilian sector, did they work on preparing on documents for the appointment and removal of commanders in the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Who were appointed and dismissed by Mr. Stojic?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes, this was done by us.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did he perform the appointments and removals in the way that you described, in the way that you interpreted the provision of Article 34?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Please take a look at the provision of Article 30 of this regulation, and then we will leave it be. In Article 30: "In the performance of tasks within his remit, commander in chief of the armed forces adopts directives, orders decisions." What we're interested in is paragraph 2: "Supreme commander of the armed forces may delegate certain tasks of leading and commanding the armed forces to the head of the Defence Department." So very specifically, I'm asking you this: Did you see a single document where the president of the HZ-HB delegate to the head of Defence Department any part of his tasks relating to the use of armed forces?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: I've never seen a single one.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Have you seen any document signed by Mr. Stojic which, by its content, would represent the commanding of armed forces or the use of armed forces?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: I've never seen a single one.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Bozic, let's take a look at document P 00586. Could you explain to the Chamber, please, what it's all about?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: This is a decision on the basis of the organisation of the Defence Department of the Croatian Defence Council of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, adopted on the 17th of October, 1992 by Mr. Mate Boban.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Bozic, when it was adopted, you had occasion to read it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: That's correct, because I worked together with my colleagues, on the basis of this decision, on the decision of the establishment and structure of the Defence Department.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: What is in paragraph 1 is not contentious, but I would like to mind your memory with respect to paragraph 2. It reads attached to the head are a military council. Do you recall this military council being established at any point in time?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: What about the chief inspectorate?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In administrative and technical terms, the head will be assisted by the cabinet of the head and general affairs and information unit as a separate organisational unit. Please, Mr. Bozic, tell us, was there any cabinet of the head of department?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: No, there was no cabinet. We wanted to establish one, but given the problems in terms of employing the right people, it was never established.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Was there any general affairs and information system department -- office?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: No, there was one person who dealt with the computer introduction, the information technology, not information system. It was being done in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: There is a deputy to the head, who is in charge of the civilian sector directly, which contains organisational units. Mr. Bozic, in January 1993, were you appointed to that position of deputy?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, since we have listed administrations within the civilian sector -- I will be specific. The Administration for Mobilisation and Military Preparation, when did it start working?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: No, it wasn't there at the beginning. It started work at the beginning of June 1993, when Mr. Dobroslav Barbaric was appointed to that administration.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: What about the civilian protection headquarters; was it ever established?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Never?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: There were discussions whether civilian protection or civilian defence should be under the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: What about the Administration for Budget or Budgeting?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: It was never established.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: What about the Administration for Legal Affairs?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Personnel Administration?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojic and I found that administration when we arrived. It was established in May 1992. We took the personnel from the Personnel Administration when the Defence Department started working.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We will come to the reports of work for 1992-1993. We will be able to read what all the administrations subordinated to you did. Mr. Bozic, let's take a look at the next document, 2D 00567. Could you please explain --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I'd like to put an administrative question to you. Several of us in this courtroom took part in a lot of meetings in the past. We know how things work. As far as you can remember, did Mr. Stojic have meetings with the various people, as mentioned in the document, as a deputy? Were there meetings which you attended? Of course, there were, but did you organise meetings to take stock of the situation with the various people in charge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were no specific or special meetings with heads of administrations. We had a body which we called a college, attended by assistant ministers, representatives of the Main Staff, I myself, and heads of certain administrations. Your Honours, as you had occasion to see and as I said, out of all the administrations listed in this regulation, the only one which functioned when this was established was the Personnel Administration, performing tasks which do not fall within the remit of a typical personnel administration, but rather working on welfare issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I got you right, within his department or ministry, Mr. Stojic was not trying to convene meetings with the various people in charge to address problems or to make decisions or to implement the policy which was outlined by the government.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to be as precise in my answer as possible. As far as the administrations made reference to here, no, there were none; but we had an informal body which we called a college, attended by assistants to Mr. Stojic, a representative of the Main Staff, heads of certain administrations, and I, as the deputy. As far as administrations referred to right now, it was impossible to meet them because they were never established.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This college you're talking about, where representatives from the headquarters were, during the meetings of this college were you talking about the military situation? Did you explain to everybody that, and this is an example I'm taking, that the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina was carrying out a breakthrough and that it was going to have consequences, in terms of refugees, for instance, that, We had to try and oppose such a breakthrough using weapons and deploying military units. Is that the kind of things you were talking about, or were you talking about something different?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, we never discussed, at our college meeting, military operations that the army was taking or was going to undertake, but we discussed administrative and expert issues, we discussed matters of structure or organisation within the department, or documents and acts we were supposed to forward to our superiors.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One technical question. You had a phone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is it a single-line telephone or was it a telephone with several keys, and by pressing one key, for instance, you could have direct access to General Petkovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, there was no such communication.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Did you have a direct line with Mr. Boban?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think no. I think that the communications system may seem strange to you today, but we had a system of communications which was barely functional. It was very difficult to maintain it and to keep its functionality.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it would be useful for me to know when I was supposed to finish. I hope --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe we could have the break now, since it's 25 to 6.00. We'll have a 25-minute break -- 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may proceed, Ms. Nozica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Bozic, I'm going to ask you to look at the next document, 2D 00567. And can you explain to the Trial Chamber what sort of a document this is?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: This is a decision on the basic principles of organisation of the Defence Department adopted by Mr. Mate Boban, and as the word says, it talks about the principles of the organisation of that department, what that should be.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Bozic, I would like -- this is something that we already discussed, this decision. This P 00586. Let's look at this other document, and that is 00567.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, this is my mistake. This is a decision on the internal organisation of the Defence Department. I was talking about the wrong document. I said that that was practically the first document that I worked on when I came to the department, and the decision regulates the internal organisation within the actual Defence Department.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Bozic, in paragraph 2, item 2 of this document, it says --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please wait until the interpreters see on the screen where she's reading from.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Chief of administration for the defence affairs and mobilisation, budget administration, civilian protection, staff legal affairs administration, personnel administration, and welfare administration manage the work of those administrations and answer for their work to the deputy head."

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It says in this decision that a special organisation was drafted for the Main Staff and that is an integral part of this decision. Mr. Bozic, did you work, first of all, on that organisation?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry. And did you ever see that structure?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't work on the organisation of the Main Staff, and I never saw it, because the Main Staff had its own administration for organisation within the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. I apologise to counsel for the interruption. I thought I heard an intervention by the interpreters, asking for a certain answer to be repeated, but perhaps I was the only one. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, thank you to my learn friend Mr. Scott. You are not the only one, actually. I was just told the same by Mr. Khan.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So when I asked you if you -- when I quoted paragraph 2, if these jobs for which these personnel persons were responsible to the deputy head, can you please tell us what you answered?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes, those are these jobs, and it's the same thing that I talked about that is contained in the decision on the basic organisation, and these heads were response -- chiefs were responsible to me as the deputy head of the Defence Department.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I asked you if you had worked on the structure and organisation of the Main Staff, and you answered that you didn't, and my second question was whether you saw that document before.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Bozic, let us now move to the next decision, and that is P 2477. It's a decision. Can you explain what this is about?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: This decision was adopted in May 1993, and what particularly it refers to this part of the civilian sector that I was heading is that here a new special administration is being introduced, an administration which did exist before, but it was within the administration, and it was working on the duties that I had already described.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bozic, can you now tell us -- we've seen the internal organisation of the Defence Department in the previous documents. Which documents regulated the position of the Defence Department within the HVO HZ-HB?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: This was a statutory decision, so it was regulated by a basic-founding document.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Bozic, can we look at that decision? This is P 00303.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: That is a decision which you say regulates the decision of the Defence Department. Was there any other decision that was adopted that was more specific about the duties and assignments of the Defence Department within the HVO HZ-HB?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: All right. As a lawyer, I must say that this is the basic act, and everything else that arises from that was adopted pursuant to this basic document. More or less, if we were to say that that would be some sort of sub-regulation, and within that structure, the commission was also working of the HVO HZ-HB.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you look in your binder at 1D 00001.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you please look at Article 9. Does Article 9 actually refer to the assignments that were in the jurisdiction of the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Counsel, I think you have made a mistake when you called the number. You called it, as it is here, "1D 0001," but it is 1D 00101, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I can see it on the screen, so evidently I have called the proper document, and that is 00001, four zeros, 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. Then the mistake seems to be in the binder. Okay, it's clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Okay, it's clear. Your D's look like an O very often, and you forgot the four O's, which is quite a lot to forget even if it's only O's. That's why I was misled. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour. I am going to warn my case manager to write more clearly so that we avoid confusion in the future.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Have you found it, Mr. Bozic?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In Article 9, I repeat my question: Are the duties of the Defence Department stated, or the duties that it should perform, because this was adopted on the 15th of May, 1992? So my question would be: Are these those assignments that the Defence Department actually executed?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And my next question is whether these are the same duties which are in the regulations on the armed forces in Article 10, which are supposed to be jobs under the jurisdiction of the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't want to compare the two texts right now, but in principle I can reply that the two texts have more or less the same content.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'm going to change my topics, which would generally be the reports about the work or the work programme drafted by the Defence Department. First of all, I'm going to ask you if you recall that the Defence Department made any kind of proposal for a work programme or a programme of work.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And how was this work programme drafted?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: In the technical sense, all the sectors would submit their programmes of work, and then there would always in the report be a section which had to do with the Main Staff and the Information Service. There would be a separate section for that. And then when all these proposals from the sectors were received about their work programmes, then we would make a summary which would be sent to the HVO HZ-HB.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Bozic, can you please tell me how the reports on the Defence Department's work were drafted?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: In the same way, when we would receive the reports on the work of each individual sector, who did what, then on the basis of their reports and -- we would make a summary report that would be submitted to the HVO HZ-HB.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you remember, please, what you specifically did, in terms of these reports? Did you have to do something in the sector where you were or who, in the end, made this summary of all the reports from all the administrations?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: In the beginning, in my civilian sector, we only had the Personnel Administration, so then they would draft their report, which would then be incorporated into a joint Defence Department report. And as I said at the beginning, the president -- the Cabinet of President Stojic [as interpreted] was not working, so that is something that I would actually work on with my colleagues from the Personnel Administration.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Bozic, you said that these reports were submitted to the HVO HZ-HB. Were you ever present at a government session or actually at the HVO HZ-HB when these reports were adopted?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I think that I did attend some of these sessions.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: According to your recollection, were these proposals discussed?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes, the submitted reports were discussed in the same way as any other item on the agenda for the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I would now like you to look at some documents, Mr. Bozic. The first document would be P 48900 -- P 04890.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. Can you please tell me what this document is about?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: This is -- these are the minutes of a meeting of the HVO HZ-HB which was held on the 8th of September, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you look at item 7, whether there is any reference to the programme of work here in this paragraph? Behind or after the agenda, there is Article 7. Do you see it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes. It says, in the agenda, basic elements for drafting a HVO plan of work -- plan of work of the HVO, the departments and the sections.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Bozic, can we look at the next document. That should be document 1D 00110.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you please tell me what sort of a document this is?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: This is the standing orders of the HVO of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna which regulates its work.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you please look at Article 8 of this document and tell us whether it was established -- in what manner are the programmes of work drafted?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right, thank you very much. Let's look at the next document, Mr. Bozic, and that is document P 00518.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me, Ms. Nozica. If I look at page 75, line 10 to 13, your question ends with: "In what manner are the programmes of work drafted?" And the answer is: "Yes." That is a bit surprising.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm going to put that question again.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In what way were the programmes of work drafted? Evidently, we have some sort of mistake here, either in my question or in your answer. I asked you in what manner were the programmes of work drafted. Listen to my question first. How were the proposals of the programme for work drafted in the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: I said that it was done in the way that each sector would make their own proposal of work, and that would be submitted to the head. And after receiving all the proposals, a summary proposal would be made. That would be a joint proposal of the work, which would then be submitted to the HVO HZ-HB for further procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you now to look at document 1D 00110. I'm going to put a precise question to you. Was there a duty on the part of the Defence Department to draft programmes of work pursuant to this article?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I already answered that question. I think that there was some problem in the interpretation, because my answer did refer to this specific Article 28 that you put your question on.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let's look at document P 00518.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is a proposal of the work programme until the end of 1992. Mr. Bozic, do you recall whether this is one of those documents that were drafted in the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is practically our first obligation that has to do with the previous HVO HZ-HB session that we looked at before, so we are submitting a report on the implemented activities pursuant to meetings from the session of the 7th of September, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Bozic, can we now look at document P 00518. Actually, it's a document that we were already looking at. Can you please look at document P 00128?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this is about? Can you remember what this is about?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: This is a report on the work of -- during 1992 that we did, and we submitted it to the HVO HZ-HB.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And now let's look at page 6 in English and Croatian, just briefly. And can you please tell us whether those parts that you drafted are cited in the report? Actually, those parts that were subordinated to you, the Personnel Administration, is being referred to here, and it is discussed here what the administration -- Personnel Administration did in that period.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the page number again?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes. It was page 6.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: It reads, in compliance with what I said, to determine all participants in the homeland war, killed and missing persons, preparation of forms, distribution to municipal headquarters, who were supposed to provide us with feedback. And since this report was submitted in March, some IT equipment is being introduced to process such data.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you take a look at the next document. These are exhibits, and we've seen this document on a number of occasions, 1D 1607. Mr. Bozic, tell me, have you found it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You were present at the 37th session of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: For the purposes of this part of your examination in chief, could you tell us in what capacity did you attend sessions of the HVO HZ-HB?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did attend certain sessions in the absence of Mr. Stojic. At some sessions, I was a rapporteur when it concerned documents that I personally worked on, together with my colleagues, and which were submitted to be adopted by the session of the HVO HZ-HB, but I was never a member of the HVO HZ-HB. I attended meetings in my capacity as deputy of Mr. Stojic, deputy head of the Defence Department.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Could you take a look at item 15 of this -- of the minutes of the meeting of the HVO HZ-HB, dated 5th of May, 1993.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In Article 15, delegrations [as interpreted] on the report of the work for 1992, and on the last page at 15, could you tell us whether this report was adopted at this session?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Bozic, it says here: "After considering all -- situation in all spheres of life in the territory and separate reports on the work and activities of the bodies and services of the HVO HZ-HB, a decision was unanimously adopted to accept the report on the work of the HVO HZ-HB for 1992."

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Bozic, since those minutes are scarce, in terms of information, was this so, as reflected in the minutes, relying on your memory; so whether first the reports were individually presented and then debated and then adopted unanimously, as it says here?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: In my previous statements during my testimony, I discussed this very matter. First, discussion was held on all matters which were included as items of the agenda, and these minutes are very rough because there were -- there was no recording -- audio- or video-recording of the proceedings, neither was there was telegramic [as interpreted] transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like you to take a look at 2D 1018.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Bozic, could you tell me, please, what this is about, and who signed it on behalf of Mr. Stojic? We're going to encounter similar documents, so let's make this clear.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: I signed it on behalf of Mr. Stojic, and it clearly states that this falls within the scope of duties of all sectors of the Defence Department and the Main Staff, pursuant to the 5th of May [as interpreted] session, that a report be prepared for the period -- the period for January and June 1993. All heads of sectors should prepare their reports of their sector.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, the date was the 5th of July, 1993, not 5th of May.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So let's take a look at this report for January and June of 1993. This is document P 49 -- P 4699. Take a look at page 14, and page 9 in the English version. The heading is "Personnel Administration." Could you briefly tell us about the characteristics for the latter part of the year from June to December?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: We managed to equip ourselves, in terms of technical equipment, to maintain the registers, collect data for professional units, and for employees of the Department of Defence and Main Staff, in the sections and offices. Practically, we started working on preparations to issue ID cards for members of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Following from this report, what would be concluded is they had already been produced, the ID cards. Please take a look at page 16, the Administration for Mobilisation and Conscription. This is one of the administrations that was subordinated to you; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: That's correct, yes, this is what I said. The Administration for Conscription and Mobilisation only started working at the beginning of June 1993, when Mr. Dobroslav Barbaric was appointed as head of that administration. And what is stated here is from the 1st of June, 1993, from when the chief of administration was appointed initially, the administration performed the following tasks.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now please take a look at the next document, P 4008.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: In this binder, there is no document.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Then you should take the other binder. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it, the first document.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Forty-ninth session of the HVO, dated 7th of August, 1993. You attended that session again. Mr. Bozic, if I'm right, it would follow that if you were in charge of an organisational sector whose report is presented, then you would go there to the session?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I sometimes acted as a rapporteur. Sometimes I stood in for Mr. Stojic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Then we are going to take a look further in the text, when the reports on January to June of 1993 are discussed.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you take a look at the paragraph at 3 and tell us what it is all about?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: What is discussed are reports of the Defence Department and other departments. It is noted here that the Defence Department report has been adopted, with a note that an additional analysis of the state of affairs was supposed to be submitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you recall what was this all about?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember, but what is demonstrable from this is that a debate was held on the report, remarks were made by members of the HVO HZ-HB to provide supplementary information, but I don't know really what they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'm referring to His Honour Antonetti's question about how decisions were taken. Please, under item C, could you tell us what is said in the report about the Justice Department?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: The report of the Justice and Administration Department of the HVO HZ-HB was rejected.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You do recall what happened?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: I can't remember the details, but the fact that the department's report was rejected or adopted, there must have been reasons for that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'm not going to dwell on that. Please take a look at the next document, P 07419. It's a report of work of the HVO for July-December 1993. It's a report which partly covers the period when Mr. Stojic was head of the Defence Department. Please take a look at the text which makes mention of the Personnel Administration, Roman numeral II. That's the fourth page. It is stated here expressly that for personnel affairs, that military ID cards were prepared within the remit of the Personnel Administration. Could you tell us something more about this period of work?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: What is indicated here, very briefly, the tasks of the Personnel Administration. A problem that I referred to on several occasions today is highlighted, and that is shortage of personnel, and they also discussed what should be prepared for the forthcoming period. What I'd like to highlight and stress is what I already said. The Administration for Welfare, which was part of my civilian sector within the Defence Department, started its work, started being organised, and started performing their works depending on the scope of their -- or terms of their reference.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'm going to show you several documents with respect to the Personnel Administration. I'm not going to ask you about the Welfare Administration, because the next witness is supposed to deal with that. But with respect to the Personnel Administration, please take a look at document 2D 01458.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You made reference to this document. Please explain the Bench what it's all about.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: As I already stated, the Personnel Administration was established on the 8th of May, 1992, almost four months before the Defence Department was established.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Please take a look at the next document in the binder, 2D 01459. We already discussed this document very briefly. Could you please explain what it's all about?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: The appointment of Mr. Dobroslav Barbaric as chief of the Conscription and Mobilisation Administration.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: What was -- please explain briefly to the Bench what was the task of the Personnel Administration when such documents were drafted and adopted.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Practically, the Personnel Administration drafted all appointment and dismissal documents which were later on signed by Head Stojic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's take a look at the next document in your binder, 2D 02011.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Could you explain the Bench, please, what this document is about?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: This is a list of eight persons who, so to speak, were part of the office of Head Stojic, headed by me. We see two military policemen, two secretaries, one clerk, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I heard you say "eight."

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Oh, I apologise. Seven. My mistake. Seven persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Bozic, this is a payroll list for December 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Asked by me previously about the number of people working at the Cabinet of the head of department --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: -- were these the persons and number of persons that you specified earlier?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let's take a look at the next document, 2D 02014.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: What is it, please?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: A payroll -- payroll list for November 1992, referring to persons employed by the Personnel Administration.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: When you take a look at this list, does it jog your memory as to which person of these was a jurist or a lawyer who helped you?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: I'm sure that Gordan Zadro was a lawyer. I'm not sure about Mr. Jozo Palac [phoen]. And for the others, I'm 100 percent sure that they were not lawyers.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: After this payroll list for November, maybe we could take a look at another document which may be interesting, and that's 2D 04016, sorry. 2D 04016. The next one should be 2D 04016. Could you please tell the Bench what this document is about?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: This is a list of personnel who worked on -- as security employees of the Defence Department.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very soon I'm going to ask you about the ethnic structure of the HVO, but let's look at December 1992. The person under the number 17, which ethnicity would that person be?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: 23, Muslim?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: 28? I don't want to speculate.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now let's take a look at 2D 0090 -- 989.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It's a proposal of the 1st Brigade of HVO, Knez Domagoj. Could you explain to the Bench what kind of document this is and what is the connection of this document with the Personnel Administration?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: The link of this document with the Personnel Administration is that pursuant to this proposal that would be received by the Defence Department after due process, the Personnel Administration would prepare documents on appointments, because if I'm allowed to read out a part of the text, this refers to the appointment to certain posts within the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you two things about this, Mr. Bozic. Are these posts which Mr. Stojic was authorised to appoint pursuant to Article 34 of the regulations of the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And on the last page, if you can remember, what was the procedure for appointment, what the Personnel Administration would receive? Would it be a proposal? Was any consent sought or required before Mr. Stojic received the document to sign?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is what I explained. A proposal would come from the unit. Consent would be obtained from the Main Staff, and then the Personnel Administration would draft the document to be signed by Mr. Stojic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'm going to show you several such documents on appointments made by Mr. Stojic. This would be, the next one would be 2D 00985.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is Eugen Kvaternik - Bugojno Brigade appointments?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: There is a long list of appointments, 80 names. You had occasion to read it, Mr. Bozic. These persons, were they those who Mr. Bruno Stojic was authorised to appoint?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you look at the next document? That would be P 10846.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is also a document of appointment. Was this absolutely in accordance with what we talked about?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The next document, can you please look at it, P 1805. All right. We have something characteristic here, and that is on the 4th of April, 1993, in the Stjepan Radic - Ljubuski Brigade, Adis Delalic was being appointed. According to his name, what ethnicity do you think he is?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: If I can say that I noticed that in the prior appointment, that is, of the 12th of April, that judging by his name and his father's name, this is a person of Muslim ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. Thank you for that remark. That also applies to the previous document, P 1846, and also this one, P 01805. Judging by the name and the name of the father, Mr. Bozic, it would seem that these were members of which ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: These are members of the Muslim ethnic group.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Bozic, I'm now going to show you one document, and that is 2D 0201, and I'm going to please ask you to comment on the contents of this document. What is this document about, and why, from this exhaustive report, can we see that some persons from the Main Staff helped in the drafting of certain documents adopted either by the Personnel Administration or the Mobilisation Administration? Can you please explain why this was necessary?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: This is what I was trying in the beginning --

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'm going to say this again, 2D 020 -- 2D 0201.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: This is what I said already once at the beginning, and that is that we were, in all of these defence sections, and I can say that this applies to all of the administrations, that we had a lack of skillful, qualified personnel, so obviously persons who were in the Main Staff who were very good at this kind of thing helped us. What is most important to note is that for all of us, work in the Defence Department was new. For the most part, we were not qualified or had any work experience, in terms of the military part of the work, so that colleagues helped us, in the professional sense, in the preparation of certain documents. So I probably think that this was the case in -- with this report that we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Document 2D 0202 -- 2D 02010. I don't know what the problem is. I think that we have the wrong document on the transcript. 2D 02010. Now it seems to be all right. Sir, now I'm going to ask you: A lot of attention was drawn by Their Honours by a document who was given to you -- that was given to you separately. It was given to Their Honours as well separately, and I think that you are the best person to be able to explain this document, and that is document 2D 00150. You have it separately. The document is separate, and I'm going to now remind you what this is about. It's a review of the ethnic structure of the members of the HVO. It's been given to the office of the president of the HVO HZ-HB, and it was drafted by the Personnel Administration, and it was dated the 9th of June, 1993. Since we discussed a lot about this, about the percentage of Croats and Muslims in the HVO units, can you please explain to Their Honours how this document was drafted and who drafted it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Well, I can only say that I'm looking at this document for the first time. Actually, the first time I saw it was during the preparation for my testimony. Evidently, it went directly from the personnel chief to the office of the president of the HZ-HB, Mr. Boban, and I can see a review of this ethnic structure. In the document, it was done on the basis of information, such as it is, when we were working on the ID cards of all the members of the HVO in the units, in the Defence Department and in the offices. All these people filled in specific forms, entering information on the basis of which the ethnicity of these people was established. This is something which, in the area of the former Yugoslavia, was usual, and in that way documents were drafted as well as personal ID cards of all of us, and this practice was adopted when the ID cards were made for members of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: When you say IDs of the HVO members, we are talking about military identification cards?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: I have to say "IDs." We, in the department, also had our own ID cards. All of us had ID cards, and you can see here at the beginning that it says that the Defence Department, including all the sectors, so the ethnic structure was reviewed in all the sectors, from the Main Staff and everywhere else, and then it ends with the units which are at the bottom of the list. The IDs were issued also to us who were not members of the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. So, Mr. Bozic, I can conclude that this was done on the basis of military ID -- excuse me, on the basis of ID cards which -- the information for which was submitted by those who are in the lists?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: Yes, the forms were filled in by those who were later issued with ID cards. Yes, that's where the information was derived from.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Bozic, can you please tell the Trial Chamber what documents were adopted by the Defence Department? Since we can see that you were quite busy with the preparation and work in the Personnel Administration for -- in the adoption of documents, can you please tell us, what sort of documents were adopted by the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: I personally am talking about our work duties pursuant to the Decree on the Armed Forces, and on the basis of these duties we adopted what I can call sub-documents, bylaws. We could refer to them like that. So when we're talking about the Decree on the Armed Forces, we would be drafting the regulations or books of rules for military conscription. We or the Defence Department made rules on the functioning and the activities of the security and intelligence services. On the other hand, we also had the duty pursuant to decisions and conclusions of the HVO HZ-HB. At this point in time, I can recall and speak about duties when the decisions on stamps and seals in the HVO were adopted, what our obligations were in the proceedings to make, register and issue those stamps. Also documents within the department, there would be a basic act adopted by the HVO HZ-HB, and our acts would -- documents would be adopted pursuant to that. We also were obliged to propose certain documents that were adopted at the level at the HVO HZ-HB or, rather, that were adopted at sessions of the HVO HZ-HB.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So here you were talking about general documents, general regulations. We often had the opportunity to see them when you were in the Personnel Department; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: I didn't think there was any need to talk about individual acts. We would prepare an act which would be adopted by the president, when we're talking about certain appointments pursuant to his authorities. I also focused more on documents that we were adopting, so to say in view of the position that we had according to our place in the organisational structure.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We're now dealing with a topic that was of interest to His Honour Judge Antonetti. If you can, can you please briefly explain how these documents were prepared in the Defence Department? This is a hypothetical question. We have a whole series of these documents. We have the procedures of how these acts were drafted, discussed about. Can you please tell us, in the end, how they were proposed, adopted, and went into effect?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: If we're talking about some documents which, in principle, were proposed by certain sectors of the Defence Department Administration, as such, they were drafted -- if we are talking about documents which referred to the complete or entire Defence Department, I would mostly be working on those types of documents with colleagues from the Personnel Administration. Drafts of such acts, whenever possible, and we managed to do that most of the time, would be put through a college procedure at the Defence Department. They would be discussed, and suggestions would be made before they would actually be drafted in the form which would then be submitted for further procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In response to Judge Antonetti's question, you explained what colleges were. Now I'm going to ask you about these discussions at the college sessions, about these acts that were supposed to be passed on for further procedure. Were general acts, bylaws, also discussed which were supposed to be signed only by Mr. Stojic, the head of the Defence Department, specifically? Were such acts also discussed at the college?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: We did discuss these acts just for the purpose of being informed about it within the department. We wanted to follow what was going on with the acts that we proposed and that were going to go on for further procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Bozic, how often were these college sessions scheduled? And we would also like to know who were members of the college and how often they sat in at meetings.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: I would first of all like to tell the Trial Chamber that the college was an informal body, and members did not have any kind of legal basis for their existence. It was an ad hoc body which had a need to discuss certain matters, certain questions that would be subject to further procedure, and would be drafted in the forms of draft laws and bylaws. So we wanted to be informed about matters that were important and about matters that were being done in the department and on behalf of the department. All the assistants of the head would attend these meetings, also representatives of the Main Staff. I, myself, was there as Mr. Stojic's deputy, as well as the chiefs of certain administrations in the department.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You explained that the college was an informal body. Did it ever happen that the college would adopt decisions or a decision?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC
utterances.text: I think that there were situations like that, when the college did adopt some decisions.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Your Honours, if you permit me, I am going to move now to a very broad topic, and I would not like to interrupt once I begin. So if you have nothing against that, I would suggest that we stop now and that we continue our session tomorrow morning -- tomorrow afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It's almost 7.00. As you know, Witness, we will resume tomorrow morning, because there will be a morning session tomorrow. We will resume at 9.00. Now, as regards the time you have used, Ms. Alaburic, you've used up two hours and thirty-five minutes -- I'm sorry, Ms. Nozica. I was thinking about Ms. Alaburic. Ms. Nozica, you've used up two hours and thirty-five minutes. Therefore, you've got two hours and twenty-five minutes left. I wish you a good evening. See you tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 3rd day of February, 2009, at 9.00 a.m.
